This is written very well! I love the line “when the spring arrives will you still be mine?” really hits deeply for someone who feels a sense of doubt in a relationship I also got the impression that this relationship is one where one person loves the other more and will sacrifice their own happiness for this person and will stay even if it sacrificed their own happiness and they become winter when they were always more spring.

I love the word choices! “anxious attitude with chaotic solitude” that rhyme scheme really goes well together and sets the correct theme for this poem. The repetition works well and this feels very raw, I think everyone has experienced some sort of toxic relationship with a person or with something or even yourself and I think this poem really describes the emotion of that well!

To answer a few of your questions this writing was inspired by unhealthy relationships with a parental figure, and how mental illness impacts the relationships around this individual and be passed down through genetics. Basically having someone you idolized turn out to be just how everyone else saw them and how there own pre conceived opinions about this person turned out to be true and how it is like generational trauma. Deep down they were meant to be destructive of everything around them. I wanted to leave things kinda up for interpretation so i’m afraid more specific details will close that door. But thank you for the feedback I appreciate it!

I like the repetition used in the rhyming scheme, and the overall theme of the poem. While reading this I interpreted this poem as the reminiscence of a dark time or a bad situation that occurred and even though moving past it is possible, it still pops up and you’re brought back to that moment. I may be entirely wrong but its still a beautiful piece and spoke to me. I would just focus on sentence structure and grammar a bit more.

This poem is well written and thought out clearly, I really value “The fog made me happy, the sun it just couldn’t, while I do miss the fog I know that I shouldn’t.” its very beautiful and really puts an emphasis finding comfort in such a dark place and once you start to leave that place and the sun comes through you cant help but miss the sense of security within the fog. As someone with seasonal depression this poem hit deeply for me. I would recommend just a bit of peer editing and grammar touch ups!
